intended_object: An internal bookkeeping device: the exponent vector of the monomial ∏_{(i,j)∈s} X_i X_j, for a finite set s of upper Gram pairs. It is the sum over pairs (i,j) of e_i + e_j, so it records how often each index occurs (a "row-degree" vector). Inferred from the docstring and from its use in `gramPairMonomial`/`gramEquationPolynomial` expansions.
explanation: The definition is `∑ z ∈ s, (Finsupp.single z.1 1 + Finsupp.single z.2 1)`. This matches the docstring: it is the sum of the exponent vectors of the Gram pairs in s. Its only role is to make two things work in the library's proof: identifying `∏_{z∈s} X_{z.1} X_{z.2}` with `monomial (gramFamilyExponent s) 1`, and computing coefficients of the expansion of `∏ (1 - X_i X_j)` in the Weyl/Gram alternant argument. It can be read as a degree sequence of an edge set, with loops counting twice. But it is a proof-specific auxiliary construction, not a standard mathematical object that the library is trying to formalize. The definition is correct for what it is used for.
